correctness.rationale: The certification gap is exact. PDNQP v1 requires Q+γ^{-1}I≻0 yet chooses γ^{-1}=−θ+δβ from a Lanczos estimate θ. For an ordinary smallest Ritz value, Rayleigh–Ritz gives θ≥λ_min(Q), so the shifted minimum is exactly δβ−(θ−λ_min). The diagonal Vandermonde family hides the negative eigendirection for any fixed Krylov budget and leaves the shifted Hessian indefinite; continuity makes failure persist on an open set of starts. The norm-only bound λ_min≥−β and θ≤β gives sufficiency of δ>2, while the 2×2 witnesses prove sharpness. The Gershgorin repair is a valid certified lower-bound construction.

originality.rationale: Lanczos misconvergence and certified extremal-eigenvalue bounds are classical, and the record correctly excludes them from novelty. The located PDNQP v1 explicitly says the Lanczos-based Eq. (11) is chosen to convexify the inner QPs but states no certified lower-bound safeguard. Searches found no public correction or prior PDNQP-specific derivation of the exact error budget, all-finite-budget open-set counterexample, or sharp δ>2 information-poor threshold.

scientific_value.rationale: Strong convexity is a stated hypothesis connecting PDNQP's practical initialization to its inner rAPDHG solver and imported proximal-ALM convergence theory. Identifying when the published initialization fails, and supplying both a sharp worst-case boundary and a cheap certificate, is a substantive correctness result for a new numerical method.

citations.note: PDNQP v1; Eq. (4) requires strong convexity and Eq. (11) uses an estimated smallest eigenvalue from Lanczos with δγ=10^-2.

findings: PDNQP v1 states Q+γ^{-1}I≻0 as the convexification condition and Eq. (11) uses a Lanczos estimate plus δγ=10^{-2}.
The explicit m=4 rational example gives θ=1/500, γ^{-1}=1/125, and shifted minimum −124/125.
For arbitrary Ritz information plus β=max(1,||Q||∞), δ>2 is necessary and sufficient for an unconditional strict-positive guarantee of this formula class.
A genuine lower bound such as Gershgorin immediately yields a factorization-free certified shift.
independent_checks: Read the current arXiv v1 HTML at the strong-convexity condition and practical proximal-selection section.
Reconstructed the diagonal Krylov/Vandermonde counterexample and open-set continuity argument.
Verified the sharp threshold inequalities and 2×2 endpoint witnesses with exact rational arithmetic.
Compared with classical Lanczos misconvergence literature and QPALM's certified-eigenvalue context.
limitations: The counterexample targets the ordinary finite-step Rayleigh–Ritz interpretation of the paper's 'Lanczos estimate'; an implementation returning a certified lower bound is outside it.
The audit does not claim the reported benchmarks fail or that the outer method necessarily diverges after an insufficient shift.
The δ>2 threshold is sharp only under the deliberately limited information model of one Ritz value plus the norm bound.
title: Sharp certification boundary for Lanczos-based proximal convexification
